forecast-period.text: A high pressure system moves southeast across waters to the south of SA, reaching the Tasman Sea later on Thursday and extends a ridge over the state until early next week. Another trough moves into the far west on Friday before weakening over the weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Possible early morning patchy frost about the southeast. Dry at first. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms developing in the far west from the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorms possibly severe with risk of damaging winds, large hail and heavy rainfall. Maximum temperatures near average, grading to below average in the northeast. Southeast to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Showers and thunderstorms in the west, contracting to the far north during the afternoon and clearing from the evening. Maximum temperatures near to above average about coastal districts, grading to below average about the northeast. Southeast to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes.

Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms about the far northwest during the afternoon and evening. Possible showers near the eastern border. Maximum temperatures above average about the south and west, tending near average in the northeast. East to northeasterly winds, tending southeasterly in the northeast, with local afternoon sea breezes.

text.p: Showers and thunderstorms developing in the west later. Possible showers near the eastern border. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average about the west coast and tending near average in the northeast. East to northeasterly winds, with local afternoon sea breezes. Winds tending north to northwesterly in the far west during the afternoon, shifting southeast to easterly during the evening.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Sunday: 1 to 5 mm about the North East Pastoral, increasing to 2 to 10 mm about the North West Pastoral. Possible falls of 10 to 20 mm about the north and west, with a chance of isolated falls of 20 to 40 mm. Less than 2 mm possible elsewhere.
